units.title: Correlate one outcome decision with an ordinary pre-write receipt
units.objective: Extend the existing pre-write wrapper with an explicit observe-only correlation that binds one immutable outcome scenario to the same real claimed-write payload, proves would-allow and would-deny signs, and preserves ordinary admission and exit behavior.

included: One typed append-only correlation receipt owned by Enforced Planning
One lazy explicit outcome-scenario path on the existing pre-write wrapper
Same-target owner-progress and synthetic circular scenarios
Focused both-sign, mismatch, failure-visibility, and exit-preservation tests
One real Enforced Planning claimed-payload observation and retained evidence
Plan, work graph, index, and roadmap reconciliation
excluded: Changes to the dependency-light ordinary claim evaluator
Claim schema, projection, mutable lease, or automatic progress classification changes
Installer, hook wiring, downstream repository, colleague, or fleet changes
Outcome blocking, shell interception, deployment, or release

outputs: Typed receipt linking one ordinary pre-write receipt to one outcome decision
Optional public wrapper path whose absence preserves current behavior
Same-payload would-allow and would-deny evidence with unchanged ordinary admission
Evidence-supported decision about durable binding or further promotion

acceptance.criterion: The ordinary pre-write decision is recorded first and remains the only authority controlling native output and exit behavior.
evidence_required: Receipt ordering and ordinary receipt ID binding
acceptance.negative_control: An ordinary denied claim remains denied even when the outcome scenario would allow.

acceptance.criterion: One typed observation binds the exact ordinary session, repository, worktree, branch, claim, target, receipt ID, and immutable scenario decision.
acceptance.negative_control: A different target or claim project produces a visible observation error without changing ordinary admission.

acceptance.criterion: The same real claimed payload produces ordinary allow in both runs, outcome would_allow for owner progress, and outcome would_deny for two synthetic non-outcome receipts.
evidence_required: Plan 116 positive and circular scenarios with identical request context
acceptance.negative_control: Approval, cost, elapsed time, and the ordinary payload remain identical; only progress receipts differ.

acceptance.criterion: The pilot makes no outcome-enforcement, automatic-lease, installer, hook-activation, shell, colleague, or fleet claim.
acceptance.negative_control: No installer, projection, claim schema, or blocking file changes appear in the submitted revision.

claim_policy.eligibility_rule: One exact live Plan 116 claim owns only the listed implementation, scenario, evidence, plan, graph, index, and roadmap paths.
